div.head: V Atr 31
div.ab: ⁊ gyf hwa forsteal oððon openne wiþercwyde ongean lahriht Christes oððe cyninges ahwar gewyrce, gylde swa wer swa wite swa lahslite, áá be ðam þe seo dæd sy.
⁊ gif hwa forsteal oððon openne wiðercwyde ongean lahriht Christes oððe cyninges ahwar gewyrce, gylde swa wer swa wite swa lahslite, áá be þam þe seo dæd sy.
⁊ gif hwa forsteal oððe openne wiðercwide ongean lahriht Cristes oððe cyninges ahwar gewyrce, gilde swa wer swa wite swa lahslite, a be þam þe seo dæd sy.
⁊ gif hwa forsteal oððe openne wiðercwide ongean lahriht Cristes oððe cyninges ahwar gewyrce, gilde swa wer swa wite swa lahslite, a be þam þe seo dæd sy.
And gyf hwa forsteal oððon openne wiþercwyde ongean lahriht Christes oððe cyninges ahwar gewyrce, gylde swa wer swa wite swa lahslite, aa be ðam þe seo dæd sy.

Und wenn einer [den Rechtsgang] sperrenden Angriff oder offenen Widerstand gegen das gesetzliche Recht der Kirche oder des Königs irgendwo verübt, zahle er entweder Wergeld oder Strafgeld, bezw. [bei Dänen] Rechtsbruchbusse, immer je nachdem die Missethat ist.

And if anyone anywhere commits obstruction [of legal process] or open resistance against the law of Christ or of the king, let him pay either wergild or fine or [among the Danes] lahslit, always according to what the deed is.
And if anyone is guilty of offering obstruction or open opposition anywhere to the law of Christ or of the king, he shall pay either wergeld or fine or lahslit according to the nature of the offence.
And if anyone commit obstruction or open resistance anywhere against the law of Christ or the king, he is to pay either wergild or fine or lahslit, ever in proportion to the deed.
And if anyone anywhere acts to obstruct or openly oppose the legal prerogatives of Christ or the king, he shall pay either wergild, a fine, or lahslit, according to the nature of the crime.

note.seg: = VI 38. Die wohl V Atr benutzende Hom. n. Wulfstan 309 bringt von c. 31 letzte Zeile, doch nur für die Kirchenrechtsverletzung durch Abgötterei
= VI 38. The Hom. n. Wulfstan 309, which probably uses V Atr, gives the last line of c. 31, but only for the violation of church law by idolatry
Zu forsteal (s. Gl Rechtsperrung 3. 4) ist ‘offener Widerstand’, was VI fortlässt, wohl nur Erklärung
With forsteal (see Gl Rechtsperrung 3. 4), ‘open resistance’, which VI omits, is probably merely an explanation
Wergeld (s. d. Gl 30. b) des Angreifers, als Strafe
Wergild (see that word in Gl 30. b) of the attacker, as a penalty
Wohl nicht 120 Schill., wie bei anderem æhlype zugunsten des Verbrechers II As 6, 3, sondern nur 30; vgl. Strafgeldfixum 6
Probably not 120 shill., as for another kind of æhlype, in favour of the criminal, II As 6, 3, but only 30; cf. Strafgeldfixum 6
Cf. E. and G. 3, 1 and note.

note.label: obstruction
note.seg: This is the original meaning forsteal, which later came to mean “lying in wait”.

note.label: lahslit
note.seg: lahslit “breach of the law” is the term given in the Danelaw to a fine varying with the rank of the offender, 10 half-marks for the king’s thegn, 6 half-marks for other landowners, 12 ores for the ceorl.
